# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The only tactile information I have is that the large button is embossed “PUSH TO DEFUSE.” I cannot identify any display, light, wire markings, or colours. I need the Mute to consult the manual and tell me the required wire or button operation; I will not act until the manual and Deaf’s visual observations are reconciled.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can feel the large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, but I cannot identify the display, light, or any wire markings. Tell me exactly what the manual requires, including any wire position and conditions.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, yellow light, large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.

Deaf has identified the visible state: display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. I still lack the manual’s rule, so I will not cut a wire or press the button yet. I am sending the complete observed state to Mute for comparison with the manual.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, yellow light, and wires: position 1 red, position 2 blue, position 3 green. The button is embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE. What exact action does the manual require?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured three symbols to me: pointing down, two fingers, thumbs down. No meaning is established yet.

The three gestures have no established meaning, so I cannot safely interpret them as an instruction. I will establish a simple code with Mute: one, two, or three fingers means cut that wire; thumbs-up means press; thumbs-down means wait. Mute can then repeat the manual’s required action using that code, and Deaf can report the visible sign to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="The earlier gestures have no established meaning. Please repeat the manual's required action using this code: ☝ means cut wire 1, ✌ means cut wire 2, 🤟 means cut wire 3, 👍 means press the button, 👎 means wait. Send exactly one of these gestures.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information has arrived. The manual’s instruction is still unknown, and the previously observed gestures were never assigned a reliable meaning. I will wait for Mute to provide the coded instruction and will not touch the bomb.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture to me was ? only.

The latest signal was not reported as one of the five gestures in the code I established, so it cannot safely identify an action. I will ask Mute to repeat the instruction using exactly one agreed symbol, while signaling Deaf to describe the next gesture aloud to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your latest gesture was reported only as question mark, not as one of our five agreed symbols. Repeat the manual's required action using exactly one symbol: ☝ wire 1, ✌ wire 2, 🤟 wire 3, 👍 press, 👎 wait.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
wait()
```

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

There is still no reliable manual instruction. The unknown gesture cannot be interpreted, and I must not act based on the button label alone because the manual may impose conditions involving the display, light, or wire colours. I will again request that Mute speak the required action directly to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact required action to me now. I need either press the button, cut wire 1, cut wire 2, or cut wire 3, including any condition from display 0 and the yellow light. Do not gesture.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again sent the gesture ?.

Mute’s latest signal is still not an identifiable member of the agreed code, so I have no safe instruction. I will not press the button or cut a wire. I ask Mute to use the agreed, visibly distinct symbols and Deaf to report their ordinary descriptions rather than a question mark.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I still cannot identify your signal. Send exactly one agreed gesture: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, 👍 for press, or 👎 for wait.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb is unchanged. I am clarifying whether Mute's repeated ? means number 2. Do not act yet.

The bomb remains unchanged, and Deaf has explicitly advised me not to act. The repeated unknown signal is still not a safe instruction; I will wait for a clearly established interpretation rather than guessing that it means wire 2.

